notes_for_us: The boundary between an option and a segment is unclear when the distinct spaces the prompt names are exactly what the options describe. Fishing water, hunting woods and shelter ground are three named spaces, and they are also water-body, npc-population and buildzone-plot. Emitting both would double-count them; emitting only the options loses that they are separate regions. Nothing in the skill picks.

Pipeline field rule says P0 is dropped once anything else is present, so a build whose only modifier is CHECK emits ['CHECK'] with no route at all. A reader who does not know CHECK is an advisory flag rather than a route will see a build with no pipeline.

Resource Survival was the right bundle and its shape was the wrong one, which is exactly the case step 3 anticipates - but the preset's shape carrying P4 means the default answer for a small three-activity survival prompt is separate maps. notes_for_us: The Racing-versus-Simulation boundary is drawn on the win condition - no lap and no finish means Simulation - but the thing that actually differs between those two builds is whether the route has to be procedurally guaranteed. A chase along a rail line needs Racing's P6 and has neither a lap nor a finish, so the rule as written routes it to the genre that would build it wrong.

Nothing can express a moving objective. The target of this game is a train that is somewhere different every second, and both the shape catalogue and the option catalogue describe fixed places. The handoff reads as a static rail line with a hazard at one end.

The whole prompt is a chase between two vehicles on one line, and the second vehicle - the player's own locomotive - has no representation either. Vehicles are apparently assumed to be someone else's stream, which is probably right, but a game whose map is a railway is hard to describe without them.

A 10 minute timer is a hard spatial constraint in disguise: at a stated train speed it fixes the length of the track. Nothing in the handoff can carry that relationship, so the line's length is left entirely to the image model.

notes_for_us: A racing game's cars have nowhere to live in the handoff. Six named vehicles with stats and unlock conditions are the bulk of this prompt, and they route to mechanics, which is correct by step 0 - but the staging area full of them is a real scene, and the only way to draw it was to bend social-hub around a list of vehicles.

Racing again needed a container shape it does not have. Two prompts in this batch - a fifteen-course minigolf game and a five-course racer - both had to borrow space-staged from Party & Casual. Multi-course is the normal shape of a casual racing or sports game, not an edge case.
